Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: issue #7689, `tests-release-and-log-analysis` close to its CI timeout

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `orchestrate-poll` matrix group-guard pattern (`if: strategy.job-index == N`, as used by `Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests (CLAUDE.md §15)`, #7575/#7579)
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one thing. Move the slowest steps of `tests-release-and-log-analysis` into the CI job with the most headroom. Keep the step bodies and the job and step names unchanged. Do not touch `timeout-minutes` and add no new required job names. This plan moves four existing steps into the idle matrix groups of `orchestrate-poll`. That follows the precedent from #7575, which put a moved step behind a single-group guard. It adds one contract-test class and one changelog fragment, and nothing else. This is not a Reduction: the full request is covered. The "complete" option costs about 30 lines of tests, so Boil the Lake does not change the scope. Those tests pin the new placement so the next budget-watch move cannot silently run these steps twice or drop them. Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the guard tests count under correctness.

### Planning ref and conflicts
- Planning ref: `main` @ `1eb3a9adcb8523601edb85ef78b9f6b705cd327f`. The `Integration branch mismatch:` line reads `unknown`, not `true`, so there is no block.
- **The step timings of run 39230958248 could not be read.** The sandbox has no network and neither `gh` nor `curl`. The steps were therefore picked by estimated cost from what the code shows:
  - Test count, and whether each test starts a subprocess (bash, git or the full poller).
  - When each step arrived. The last four steps of the job were moved in by #7383 and #7677.
  - The job measured 535–604 s on 2026-10-12, before those moves. It now takes 17m51s.
- The issue says to move steps "into the CI job with the most headroom". No current duration has been measured for any single test job:
  - Every recent budget-watch issue (#7366, #7383, #7406, #7560, #7575, #7576, #7677) recorded its job at 15–20 minutes.
  - The test jobs have been passing steps back and forth.
  - The only groups not already carrying extra work are groups 2 and 3 of the `orchestrate-poll` matrix. Group 0 carries the fast-fail subset and the single-file modules; group 1 carries the merge-train step. #4707 measured about 5 minutes per poll quarter, and the ci.yml comment says so.
  - The `orchestrate-poll` job is still one job id and one set of required check names (`orchestrate-poll (0..3)`). No new required job name is created.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`
- `changelog.d/7689-ci-release-job-step-move.md`

## Functions or modules to implement

1. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: cut these four steps from `tests-release-and-log-analysis`. Today they sit at the end of that job, around lines 1888–1925. Name, `run:` body and their absence of `env:` all stay byte-identical:
   - `Orchestrator judges on the Claude engine tests (Phase 5c)`: 48 tests, 28 subprocess calls, temp git repos.
   - `Validation harness sandbox tests`: 103 tests, bash-heavy (58 bash references).
   - `Promote cycle and blocked-verdict unit tests`: 5 modules, about 119 bash-driven tests. `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_promote_cycle.py` runs the full poller subprocess through `tests.test_orchestrate_poll_process._run_poller` for each of its 24 tests. This step is the most likely cause of the jump from about 16 to 17m51s after #7677.
   - `Review-blocked judge label propagation contract test`: 79 tests, 18 git references.

   Paste them at the end of the `orchestrate-poll` job, after `Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests (CLAUDE.md §15)`, with one added `if:` line each:
   - Group 2 (`if: strategy.job-index == 2`): `Promote cycle and blocked-verdict unit tests` and `Review-blocked judge label propagation contract test`. Both came in with #7677, and the promote module is poller-driven, the same topic as this job.
   - Group 3 (`if: strategy.job-index == 3`): `Orchestrator judges on the Claude engine tests (Phase 5c)` and `Validation harness sandbox tests`. Both came in with #7383.

   The `if:` is needed because `orchestrate-poll` is a 4-way matrix. Without it each step would run four times per CI run. Run once per CI run is the behaviour these steps had before, and it matches the merge-train precedent.

   Replace the two "Moved from …" comment blocks in the release job with one comment block above the moved steps in `orchestrate-poll`. That comment should say:
   - The steps came from `tests-release-and-log-analysis`, which took 17m51s of its 20 minutes on `main` (run 39230958248, budget-watch issue #7689).
   - Earlier origins: #7383 from `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`, #7677 from `tests-promote-stall-and-review`.
   - Step timings were not readable, so the steps were chosen by estimated cost.
   - Groups 0 and 1 already carry extra steps, so these go into groups 2 and 3.
   - None of them needs git history beyond `HEAD`, Node, or the prepared `.claude/` live copies. `orchestrate-poll` checks out at depth 1, and every git use in these modules is a temp repo or a text assertion. This was checked: the only `origin/main` references are a temp-repo `update-ref` and a string assertion.
   - The job has the same pip set and Python 3.12 as the release job.

   Keep the release job's `Checkout repository` with `fetch-depth: 0`. `SessionStart hook repo-slug contract test`, which stays in that job, needs it.

2. **`tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`**: add a `MovedReleaseStepsContractTest` class next to `MergeTrainStepContractTest`, reusing `poll_job_step`, `POLL_JOB_ID` and `CI_WF`. It has a constant `MOVED_RELEASE_STEPS = {step name: (expected group index, tuple of literal module paths)}` and these checks:
   - Each step's `if` equals `strategy.job-index == <n>`.
   - The only job that owns each step is `orchestrate-poll`. This is the same owner scan as `test_step_keeps_its_name_job_and_group_guard`.
   - Each step's `run` still names every original module path literally:
     - `tests/test_orchestrator_judges_claude_engine.py`
     - `tests/test_validation_harness_sandbox.py`
     - `tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py`
     - `tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py`
     - `tests/test_auto_release_stable.py`
     - `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_promote_cycle.py`
     - `tests/test_implement_blocked_verdict_terminalizes.py`
     - `tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py`
   - No moved step is guarded to group 0 or group 1, which already carry extra load.
   - Every guard index is less than the matrix group count (`poll_group_count()` or the equivalent existing helper around line 90), so a later shrink of the matrix cannot leave a step that never runs.

3. **`changelog.d/7689-ci-release-job-step-move.md`**: a `<!-- changelog: changed -->` fragment in the same shape as `7677-ci-promote-stall-job-step-move.md`. It should cover:
   - A step → new job (group) table.
   - The trigger: 17m51s of 20 minutes, run 39230958248, issue #7689.
   - That timings could not be read, so the choice is estimated.
   - That no job was added or renamed and no `timeout-minutes` changed.
   - That a failure in these tests now shows up under the check-run `orchestrate-poll (2)` or `orchestrate-poll (3)`.
   - That operators have nothing to do.

## Data structures affected
- The step lists of the `tests-release-and-log-analysis` and `orchestrate-poll` jobs in `ci.yml`.
- A new test constant `MOVED_RELEASE_STEPS` in the test module.
- Nothing at runtime, no state, no schemas.

## API or interface changes
- None to the external interface. The required status `CI / lint` (the `lint` aggregate) and its `needs` list do not change.
- Check-run attribution changes: these four steps' failures now appear under `orchestrate-poll (2)` / `orchestrate-poll (3)` instead of `tests-release-and-log-analysis`.

## Decisions

### D1 — Destination job: `orchestrate-poll` groups 2 and 3
- **Chosen:** `orchestrate-poll`, matrix groups 2 and 3, behind `if: strategy.job-index == N`.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`: received six steps in #7576 and #7677, and was last recorded at about 15 minutes.
  - `tests-promote-stall-and-review`: hit 16m06s (#7677).
  - `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`: hit 15m52s (#7575).
  - `static-checks`: hit 15m18s of a 15-minute budget.
  - Raising `timeout-minutes`, or adding a new job: both forbidden by the issue.
- **Why:**
  - Every single test job has a recent budget-watch record at or above the 15-minute warning line.
  - Groups 2 and 3 run only their quarter of the poll module and have no extra steps today.
  - The job id and its check names already exist.
  - The single-group guard has precedent (#7575) and is already pinned in the tests.

### D2 — Which steps move: the four steps added by #7383 and #7677
- **Chosen:** the four steps that #7383 and #7677 moved into the release job.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - The coverage gates (collector, analyzer, scenario trace). `test_ci_inventory_parity_order_contract.py` pins the collector and analyzer gates to the job that holds `Inventory parity`, so they cannot move alone.
  - `Release CI gate tests`: a fast stub-`gh` loop.
  - `Semantic cache unit tests`: pure Python, no subprocess.
- **Why:**
  - These four are the most subprocess-heavy steps in the job (full poller runs, bash scripts, temp git repos).
  - They are what grew the job from about 10 minutes to 17m51s.
  - Moving them restores roughly the job layout that measured 535–604 s, give or take the steps that moved out since.
  - Steps that #4707 put in this job stay put.

### D3 — Split the four across two groups instead of one
- **Chosen:** two steps in group 2 and two in group 3.
- **Alternatives considered
